Appearance:
MR.HIREN M MODI(3732) for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Malubhai Somabhai Khambhala (Rabari) vs Bharatbhai Virjibhai Sorthiya on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68895102/
1 MR CHIRAYU A MEHTA(3256) for the Defendant(s) No. 5 MR KRUNAL R SAKSENA(5915) for the Defendant(s) No. 3 RULE SERVED for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2,4 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MS. JUSTICE VAIBHAVI D. NANAVATI  Date : 15/02/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
By way of present appeal, the appellant herein is aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Kachchh at Gandhidham NEUTRAL
CITATION
JUDGMENT DATED: 15/02/2023 undefined in MACP No. 271 of 2016 dated 1.12.2018 wherein the tribunal awarded Rs.6,06,008/- towards compensation in favour of the original claimant

. 
2. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid amount of compensation granted by the tribunal, the appellant herein has approached this Court, seeking enhancement to the tune of Rs. 6 lakh.

3. Heard Mr. Hiren Modi, learned advocate for the appellant, Mr. Krunal Saksena, learned advocate for respondent No.3- Insurance Company and Mr. Chirayu Mehta, learned advocate for respondent No.5- Insurance Company.
4. The brief facts leading to the filing of the present appeal reads thus:
4.1
The appellant herein preferred the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 and has prayed to grant compensation of Rs.12,00,000/-.

4.2 On 23.6.2016 at around 11:30 hrs, the appellant was coming from Bhuj to Vamka via Bhachau and travelling in Toofan bearing registration No. GJ-03-AV-4993 which was being driven by opponent No.4 and when the Toofan Jeep reached near Navagam Bus Station, at that time, the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1353/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/02/2023 undefined respondent No.1 who was driving Bolero Jeep bearing registration No. GJ-12-BR-5029, in rash and negligent manner,
dashed with the Toofan Jeep.
Thus, the accident occurred in which the appellant sustained injuries.

5. Mr. Hiren Modi, learned advocate appearing for the appellant submitted the following:
(A) It is submitted that the tribunal erred in considering the income of the appellant at Rs.4000/- per month.
It was submitted that the tribunal ought to have considered the income of the appellant at Rs.10,000/- per month for the reason that the appellant was doing Animal Husbandry.

sentences.text: (B) The tribunal erred in considering the disability at 35%.
It was submitted that the tribunal erred in not considering the prospective income at 40%.

It was submitted that the tribunal ought to have granted higher amount of compensation under the head of Pain, shock and suffering, Special Diet and transportation charges and attendant charges and ought to have considered loss of amenities qua the appellant herein.

(C) Placing reliance on the aforesaid submissions, Mr. Hiren Modi, learned advocate appearing for the appellant submitted that the tribunal ought to have granted the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1353/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/02/2023 undefined compensation as claimed for to the tune of Rs.6 lakh.

6. Per contra, Mr. Krunal Saksena, learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.3 opposed the same and submitted that the compensation granted by the tribunal was just and proper and that no interference is called for in the order impugned.
It was submitted that in absence of any evidence on record, the income which was calculated at Rs.4000/- per month was just and proper and that no interference was called for.

It was submitted that the tribunal has rightly considered 35% disability for the reasons that the appellant at the time of hearing on his own volition submitted that the appellant had no objection in considering 35% disability as body as a whole.
It was submitted that the enhancement as claimed for, by the appellant, not be considered since error could said to have been committed by the tribunal.
7. This Court has gone through R&P and also heard the submissions advanced by the learned advocates for the respective parties.

8. This Court is inclined to consider Minimum Wages at the time when the accident occurred in accordance with the Schedule which has been placed on record by the learned advocate appearing for the appellant.
Considering the same, minimum wages for a duration NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1353/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/02/2023 undefined between 1.10.2015 to 31.3.2016, are to be calculated at Rs.7444/-.
In view of this Court, the same be considered at Rs.7500/-

This Court has also gone through the deposition and the cross-examination of the appellant wherein from the record it transpires that the appellant actually underwent serious injuries on head as well as bodily injuries.
In view of this Court, the actual loss of income is required to be considered for four months.

Considering the nature of the injuries, though the leg is not amputated , it can be borne from the record that the appellant actually has undergone serious injuries and the same would have resulted in loss of actual income and the Court is inclined to consider 40% towards the loss of prospective income.
9. Considering the aforesaid, the compensation qua the head of the pain, shock and sufferings be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Special Diet and transportation charges is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
The appellant herein, in view of this Court, is entitled to loss of amenities for the injuries which the appellant has undergone and the same be considered at Rs.25,000/-.

The tribunal has awarded the compensation amount of Rs. 6,06,008/-.
Thus, the amount of compensation is enhanced to Rs.5,43,820/-.

The appellant is entitled to enhanced NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1353/2019 JUDGMENT DATED: 15/02/2023 undefined compensation of Rs.5,43,820/- @
6% from the date of filing of the claim petition.

The respondent No.3 Insurance Company to deposit the said enhanced amount within a period of eight weeks from the receipt of the Order and tribunal shall disburse the same in favour of the claimant on proper verification within a period of four weeks.
In the result, the appeal stands partly allowed.
The impugned judgment and award dated 1.12.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Kachchh at Gandhidham in MACP No. 271 of 2016 stands modified to the aforesaid extent.
